title: Model-change thermostat and statistical lifeguard for safe A/B rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We need a single, configurable framework that safely manages progressive traffic for model variants (canaries/A-B/shadow) while continuously validating quality and performance. Current rollouts are manual, inconsistent across teams, and rely on ad-hoc checks.

Proposal: Implement a two-part system: (1) a traffic thermostat controller that incrementally adjusts exposure based on multi-signal health, cost, and SLOs; (2) a statistical lifeguard that runs continuous sequential checks (quality + safety + latency) and triggers automated throttles or full rollback. This ticket defines the product spec, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the first-phase MVP targeting text-generation model versions on Hosted and Dedicated deployments.
success_metrics: Reduce manual rollback incidents during model upgrades by >= 60% within first quarter of rollout
Average time-to-detect regression reduced to < 15 minutes for high-severity metric deviations
Enable teams to complete a controlled canary from 0->20% traffic without manual intervention in >= 90% of runs
False positive rollback rate under automated policy < 5% after calibration
acceptance_criteria: Console: New 'Variant Thermostat' config UI that lets PM/Eng set target metric(s), primary and guardrail signals, max step, min step, cooldown window, and emergency-stop rules.
API: rollout config schema accepted by Redwood API (config snapshot persists to rollout-history).
Controller: thermostat service that can increase/decrease traffic in bounded steps (default max step 10% every 30 minutes), honoring customer commit tiers and capacity policies.

Statistical lifeguard: continuous sequential testing pipeline that evaluates configured metrics (e.g., top-1 hallucination rate, latency p95, perplexity delta) with pre-specified alpha spending and minimum sample constraints.

Rollback: when lifeguard signals a severe regression (stat sig + effect size threshold OR SLO breach), controller automatically returns traffic to baseline and creates an incident with attached diagnostic snapshot.
Shadow mode: support for configurable shadowing of X% of traffic for offline comparison and metric collection without affecting user experience.
Telemetry: dashboards showing live thermostat state, per-metric p-values, rolling effect sizes, and recent rollouts; alert hooks into paging for high-severity events.
E2E tests: simulated rollouts with injected regressions to validate automatic throttle and rollback paths in staging.
rollout_spec: Phase 1 (MVP): Hosted + Dedicated; core thermostat + lifeguard + console controls; limit to text-generation endpoints; RBAC gated for org admins.
Phase 2: Add per-route presets, support for embeddings/rerankers, per-customer customization, integration with Dedicated autoscaler to manage capacity alongside exposure.
Default exposure policy: start 1% -> monitor 30m -> if green, step to 5% -> monitor 1h -> step to 10% -> monitor 2h -> step to 20%; all steps bounded by 'max_step' and 'cooldown' settings.
Emergency rollback: immediate 0% exposure if any of the emergency-stop rules fire (latency SLO > 2x baseline p95 for >5m, or safety metric above configured threshold with stat sig).
Shadow traffic: mirror 5-30% configurable; metrics computed offline and visible in console with replay tooling for token-level diffs.
technical_notes: Statistical design: adopt group-sequential / alpha-spending approach plus an SPRT-style signal for rapid detection. For low-signal metrics (safety events), use Bayesian hierarchical smoothing across cohorts to stabilize estimates.
Multiple comparisons: apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control across monitored metrics + cohorts; expose per-metric adjusted p-values in the UI.

Hybrid thresholds: require both statistical signal (adjusted p < 0.01 for P0 signals, 0.05 for P1) AND practical effect size (relative delta > X% or absolute delta > Y units) to trigger automated rollback.
Integration: thermostat controller subscribes to metric stream (Prometheus/OTEL + feature events) and makes deterministic exposure decisions recorded by the control plane with immutable audit logs.
Safety: limit automated reductions to not exceed customer SLAs (eg. enterprise configs may require manual approval for full rollback).
Performance: algorithm must evaluate decisions within 30s wall time; implement incremental aggregators to avoid re-scanning buckets.

Config example (YAML string to be parsed by API):
- name: thermostat_alpha
  metrics:
    - name: hallucination_rate
      primary: true
      effect_size_threshold: 0.02
      alpha: 0.01
    - name: p95_latency_ms
      guardrail: true
      effect_size_threshold: 0.25
  max_step_pct: 10
  min_step_pct: 1
  cooldown_min: 30
  emergency_rules:
    - name: latency_slobreach
      duration_min: 5
      multiplier: 2.0
Data retention: keep per-rollout fine-grained traces and diffs for 90 days for incident debugging (configurable).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: automated rollback may be too aggressive and cause unnecessary thrashing. Mitigation: require combined criteria (stat sig + effect size + cooldown), introduce a 'soft-throttle' step before a full rollback.
Risk: noisy metrics cause false alarms. Mitigation: hierarchical smoothing and minimum sample thresholds; allow teams to pin metrics to 'monitor-only' mode during calibration.
Risk: team trust and change management. Mitigation: audit trails, easy manual override, staged rollout to internal canary orgs and opt-in in console.
Risk: interplay with Dedicated autoscaler creating capacity flips. Mitigation: coordinate with autoscaler via a handshake protocol and capacity reservations for planned exposure steps.
